name: Rage in the Cage (2017)

date.source: the card's own infobox and its own opening line

appearances.note: Booked into match 3, then withdrawn by an in-fiction attack before the card per the card's own background section.

notes: A card, not a results page: seven matches plus a pre-show, every one of them a steel-cage match, and no dedicated results article was ever written. Two outcomes survive anyway, both from wrestlers' own bio pages written after the fact: Made in Detroit winning the first OWA Tag Team Championship on the kickoff, and Angelita Henderson winning the OWA Women's Championship from Erin Spencer-Wolfe in the card's second match. The other six matches are structured from the card itself with no winner recorded.

matches.note: Pre-show. No result survives anywhere in the held record.
The two had been feuding since February 2017 per Alex Madsen's own bio. No result survives anywhere in the held record.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the OWA Women's Championship
matches.note: Angelita Henderson's own bio: "On February 26, 2017 at the Rage in the Cage pay per view, Angelita defeated Erin Spencer in a steel cage match to become the new OWA Women's Champion." The title's own championship ledger (last revised 19 January 2017, before this show) still reads Erin Spencer-Wolfe as champion — the discrepancy is a stale ledger, not a contradiction; Angelita's bio is the later and more specific document.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the Women's #1 Contendership
matches.note: Originally a sixth participant was to be Abigail Dresden; the card's own background section reports her withdrawn by injury and replaced before the show. No result survives anywhere in the held record.

matches.stipulation: Triple Threat Tornado Steel Cage Match for the OWA Tag Team Championship
matches.note: Brett Edgar's own bio card reports the result: Edgar and Shane Miller, as Made in Detroit, beat Jake Anderson & Duke Knight and the Connolly Bros to become the first-ever OWA Tag Team Champions. This is the only Rage in the Cage result the wing's tier-2 read had found.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the OWA Universal Championship
matches.note: Adam Dunn had won a Fatal Four Way on the 9 February 2017 Anarchy to earn this shot. No result survives anywhere in the held record.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the OWA Intercontinental Championship
matches.note: The card bills Wolfe "(w/ Erin Spencer)" — Erin Spencer-Wolfe accompanied him to this match, in addition to wrestling her own title defense earlier on the same card (match 2). No result survives anywhere in the held record.

matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the OWA World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Gage earned this shot by attacking Chandler during a Champion vs. Champion match on the 30 January 2017 Anarchy. No result survives anywhere in the held record.

name: Anarchy (2 March 2016)

date.source: the federation's own show article and both of its championship ledgers

evidence.note: The show article's own history section: “Anarchy held it's debut show on March 2, 2016 where the first-ever OWA Heavyweight Champion was crowned in an open battle royal… The first-ever OWA Women's Champion was also crowned.”
The Heavyweight title ledger dates Tyler Chandler's inaugural reign to this show.
The Women's title ledger dates Clarissa Evans's inaugural reign to this show.

notes: The federation's own first show. No card or results document survives for it; both of the championships it crowned are ledgered to it.

name: OWA Live Event (18 January 2017)

date.source: the federation's own championship ledgers, three of which date an inaugural reign to it

evidence.note: Ledgers Mason Wolfe's inaugural Intercontinental reign to an “OWA Live Event” on this date, won in a Fatal Five Way.
Wolfe's own bio names the Fatal Five Way's other four entrants: Antonio DeLuca, Jake Anderson, Owen Grady and Ryan Henderson, with Wolfe himself the “mystery opponent” who won.
Ledgers Owen Grady's inaugural Universal reign to the same event, defeating Mitch McGillicutty.
Ledgers Erin Spencer-Wolfe's Women's Championship win to the same event, in a Six Pack Challenge.

Erin Spencer-Wolfe's own bio names the Six Pack Challenge's other five entrants: Clarissa Evans, Kasey Marie, Brooklyn Chandler, Lexie Banks and Natia Anafili, and dates the show to “January 17, 2017” rather than the championship ledgers' 18th.
Adam Dunn's own bio: a Triple Threat #1 Contenders match for the Heavyweight Championship at this show, also involving Chris Dunn and Alex Madsen, which Madsen won.
Chandler's own bio corroborates the Triple Threat and independently dates the show to “January 17, 2017.”

notes: The untitled live event that restarted the federation after its hiatus and crowned three champions in one night, plus a Triple Threat #1 contenders match for the fourth (Heavyweight) title. No card or results document survives for it. Three of the federation's own championship ledgers date it to 18 January 2017; three separate wrestler bios (Chandler's, Wolfe's, Spencer-Wolfe's) date the same show to 17 January 2017. Recorded as the disagreement it is — the date below follows the ledgers, the more numerous and more directly on-point sources.

name: Anarchy (9 March 2016)

date.source: the federation's own show-history article and three of its wrestlers' own bios, all dating the same episode a week after the 2 March 2016 debut

evidence.note: The show article's own history section: "On the March 9, 2016 episode of Anarchy, the first-ever singles OWA Heavyweight Championship match took place between Chandler and Adam Dunn. That same night there were also a series of matches to determine the #1 Contender for the Heavyweight Championship with the final match being a Fatal Four Way. Laifai Anafili would win the Fatal Four Way to become the #1 Contender. A Fatal Four Way match also took place to determine the new #1 Contender for the OWA Women's Championship which was won by Brooklyn Chandler."
Adam Dunn's own bio: "A week later on the March 9, 2016 episode of Anarchy, Adam was rewarded with a one on one championship opportunity against Chandler but once again came up short."
Chandler's own bio: "A week later on the March 9, 2016 episode of Anarchy Chandler would successfully defend the championship against Dunn."

Erin Spencer-Wolfe's own bio: "The following week Spencer would go on to defeat a returning Rebekah Dunn who was revealed as her mystery opponent to advance to the Fatal Four Way #1 Contenders Match for the OWA Women's Championship later that night. Spencer would again come up short in the Fatal Four Way after Brooklyn Chandler pinned Kasey Marie."

notes: The federation's own second show, a week after its debut. No card or results document survives for it; four match outcomes survive across three later wrestler bios and the show's own history article: Tyler Chandler's successful singles defense against Adam Dunn, Laifai Anafili's win of a Heavyweight #1 contender Fatal Four Way (three further entrants unnamed), Erin Spencer-Wolfe's win over Rebekah Dunn, and Brooklyn Chandler's win of a Women's #1 contender Fatal Four Way over Kasey Marie and Erin Spencer-Wolfe (a fourth entrant unnamed).

name: Anarchy (23 January 2017)

date.source: the federation's own show-history article, dating the returning weekly show's own restart to this date

evidence.note: The show article's own history section: "The return of Anarchy took place on January 23, 2017 where a Triple Threat #1 Contenders match took place between Angelita Henderson, Clarissa Evans and Lexie Banks. The match was won by Henderson. Anarchy General Managers Daniel Riley and Mariella Riley made a huge announcement and unveiled the brand new OWA United Kingdom Championship as well as revealed that a 32 Man Tournament would take place. Tyler Chandler successfully defended his OWA World Heavyweight Championship against Alex Madsen."

The card's own background section: "On the January 23, 2017 episode of Anarchy a #1 Contenders match took place to determine who would challenge Mason Wolfe for the OWA Intercontinental Championship. Chris Dunn won the match to become the #1 Contender. Also on the January 23, 2017 episode of Anarchy, Angelita Henderson became the #1 Contender for the OWA Women's Championship."

Adam Dunn's own bio names the Intercontinental match's shape and a second entrant: "Dunn came up short in a Four Way Elimination #1 Contenders match for the OWA Intercontinental Championship with his brother, Chris winning the match after accidentally Superkicking his own brother and forcing his elimination."

notes: The show that restarted weekly Anarchy after the January 2017 live event. No card or results document survives for it. Four outcomes survive across later documents: Angelita Henderson's win of a Triple Threat over Clarissa Evans and Lexie Banks for the Women's #1 contendership; the OWA United Kingdom Championship's own unveiling, with its 32-man tournament announced; Tyler Chandler's successful Heavyweight defense against Alex Madsen; and Chris Dunn's win of a Four Way Elimination over his own brother Adam Dunn (eliminated by an accidental superkick) for the Intercontinental #1 contendership, two further entrants unnamed.

name: Anarchy (30 January 2017)

date.source: the federation's own Rage in the Cage background section, dating this episode a week after the 23 January 2017 restart

evidence.note: The card's own background section: "On the January 30, 2017 episode of Anarchy during a Champion vs. Champion match between Owen Grady and Tyler Chandler the latter was attacked by a hooded figure before they were revealed to be new OWA signee, Hunter Gage who proceeded to lay out the champion. Six days later on OWA's official Twitter account it was revealed that Gage would challenge Chandler for the championship at Rage in the Cage after Chandler demanded the match."

notes: No card or results document survives for it. A Champion vs. Champion match between Owen Grady and Tyler Chandler was interrupted by an attack revealing Hunter Gage's arrival — the match itself is not formally ruled anywhere in the held record, and is recorded here as unresolved rather than guessed. The attack is the angle that set up Gage's Heavyweight challenge at Rage in the Cage.

name: Anarchy (9 February 2017)

date.source: the federation's own Rage in the Cage background section

evidence.note: The card's own background section: "On the February 9, 2017 episode of Anarchy, Adam Dunn defeated Laifai Anafili, Antonio DeLuca and Aaron Keller in a Fatal Four Way to become the #1 Contender for the OWA Universal Championship and will face Owen Grady for the championship at Rage in the Cage."

notes: No card or results document survives for it. One outcome survives, in Rage in the Cage's own background section: Adam Dunn's win of a Fatal Four Way over Laifai Anafili, Antonio DeLuca and Aaron Keller for the Universal #1 contendership.

name: Anarchy (23 February 2017)

date.source: Ethan Williams's own bio, dating his in-ring debut to this episode

evidence.note: Williams's own bio: "Williams officially made his in-ring debut on the February 23, 2017 episode of Anarchy as the opponent for Hunter Gage as chosen by Tyler Chandler in a Pick Your Poison match. Williams would win the match after a distraction from Chandler."

notes: No card or results document survives for it. One outcome survives, in Ethan Williams's own bio: his debut win over Hunter Gage in a Pick Your Poison match, Gage having been chosen as his opponent by Tyler Chandler and the finish coming off a Chandler distraction.
